newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson to begin offer for Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson to begin offer for Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co said Monday it intends to begin an exchange offer for all outstanding shares of Great Western Financial Corp.
Ahmanson said it would swap not less than 1.10 Ahmanson shares and not more than 1.20 for each Great Western share.

Ahmanson said it is proceeding to file with the Securities and Exchange Commission documents relating to the offer and intends to begin the offer as soon as the SEC declares the registration statement effective.

Ahmanson said Great Western shareholders will be able to tender their shares at the exchange ratio stated in its March 17 merger proposal. Under those terms, as of the close of trading May 9, Ahmanson would exchange 1.2 of its shares for each share of Great Western, representing an implied value of $47.25 per Great Western share.

Ahmanson said the ratio will be fixed within the 1.10-1.20 share range by dividing $50 by the average closing price of Ahmanson shares during the 20-day trading period ending on the third trading day preceding the expiration date of the offer, or as otherwise agreed in a merger pact with Great Western.
Ahmanson said it expects the comtemplated timing of its proposed transaction with Great Western to remain unaffected by the exchange offer.

It said it expects that if the holders of a majority of Great Western shares do not support the company's proposed merger with Washington Mutual Inc, then Great Western directors would be "compelled by their fiduciary duty" to deactivate a poison pill once a majority of outstanding shares are tendered to Ahmanson.

"Ahmanson's decision to move to the exchange offer gives Great Western stockholders an opportunity to express their support for our merger proposal," Ahmanson Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Rinehart said in a statement. "We are confident that our offer represents superior value for Great Western stockholders."
Rinehart said he is confdient an Ahmanson-Great Western merger will be more efficient and in a stronger market position than a Great Western combination with Washington Mutual.
He also said Great Western had refused to discuss Ahmanson's proposal and had "obfuscated the facts and issues."
Great Western shares were up 1-1/8 to 44-3/4 in early Monday trading.
Ahmanson was up 1/8 to 39-1/2. Washington Mutual was up 9/16 to 52-3/4.
